name: Theory of Computation
description: Formal languages, automata theory, computability, and complexity classes.

professors.name: Dr. Sarah Chen
recentComments: Challenging but fair. Lectures are well-organized and she explains concepts clearly.
Heavy workload but the material is fascinating. Definitely learned a lot.
Great at explaining complex theory. Office hours are very helpful.

professors.name: Prof. Michael Rodriguez
recentComments: Very knowledgeable but lectures can be dry. Homework is tough but fair.
Expects a lot from students but provides good feedback on assignments.
Theory-heavy course, but he makes it interesting when discussing real applications.

name: Programming Languages
description: Syntax, semantics, type systems, and paradigms of programming languages.

professors.name: Dr. Emily Watson
recentComments: Amazing professor! Makes programming languages fun and accessible.
Clear explanations and great examples. Projects are challenging but rewarding.
Best CS professor I've had. Really cares about student understanding.

name: Advanced Operating Systems
description: Advanced topics in OS design: scheduling, memory management, virtualization.

professors.name: Prof. David Kim
recentComments: Excellent at explaining OS concepts. Labs are well-designed.
Challenging material but very rewarding. Great preparation for industry.
Clear expectations and helpful during office hours.

name: Distributed Systems
description: Consistency models, consensus algorithms, fault tolerance, and distributed storage.

professors.name: Dr. Lisa Thompson
recentComments: Fascinating course on distributed systems. Dr. Thompson is passionate about the subject.
Group projects are challenging but teach real-world skills.
Great balance of theory and practical applications.

name: Cloud Computing
description: Cloud architectures, containerization, serverless computing, and DevOps practices.

name: Computer Vision
description: Image processing, feature extraction, object detection, and deep learning for vision.

name: Deep Learning
description: Neural network architectures, backpropagation, CNNs, RNNs, and transformers.

name: Natural Language Processing
description: Text processing, language models, parsing, machine translation, and sentiment analysis.

name: Reinforcement Learning
description: Markov decision processes, Q-learning, policy gradients, and deep RL.

name: Senior Capstone I
description: First semester of the two-semester senior capstone project sequence.

name: Senior Capstone II
description: Second semester of the senior capstone; final project completion and presentation.

name: Independent Research
description: Faculty-supervised independent research project in a specialized CS area.

name: Numerical Analysis
description: Floating-point arithmetic, interpolation, numerical integration, and differential equations.

name: Real Analysis
description: Rigorous treatment of limits, continuity, differentiation, and integration.

name: Topology
description: Metric spaces, continuity, compactness, connectedness, and fundamental groups.

name: Graph Theory
description: Graph properties, trees, coloring, flows, matchings, and algorithmic applications.

name: Philosophy of Mind
description: Consciousness, intentionality, functionalism, and the mind-body problem.

name: Logic and Reasoning
description: Formal logic, deductive and inductive reasoning, fallacies, and argumentation.

name: World Literature
description: Survey of major literary works across cultures and historical periods.

name: Modern Fiction
description: 20th and 21st century fiction including modernism, postmodernism, and contemporary voices.

name: History of Science and Technology
description: Development of scientific thought and technology from antiquity to the digital age.

name: Cultural Anthropology
description: Cross-cultural studies of social organization, beliefs, and human diversity.

name: Race, Class, and Technology
description: Sociological analysis of how technology intersects with race, class, and inequality.

name: Introduction to Global Studies
description: Globalization, international relations, and transnational issues from multiple perspectives.

name: Modern World History
description: Global history from 1500 to the present with emphasis on interconnection and change.

name: Artificial Intelligence
description: Search, knowledge representation, planning, probabilistic reasoning, and machine learning.

name: Compilers
description: Lexical analysis, parsing, semantic analysis, optimization, and code generation.

name: Abstract Algebra
description: Groups, rings, fields, homomorphisms, and applications to coding theory.

name: Ethics in Technology
description: Ethical frameworks applied to AI, privacy, intellectual property, and digital society.

name: Introduction to Computer Science
description: Fundamental concepts of computing, problem-solving, and introductory programming.

name: Programming Fundamentals
description: Core programming constructs: loops, functions, recursion, and basic data structures.

name: Data Structures
description: Lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, hash tables, and their algorithms.

name: Discrete Mathematics
description: Logic, sets, relations, functions, combinatorics, and graph basics for CS.

name: Algorithms
description: Algorithm design and analysis: divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy, NP-completeness.

name: Computer Organization
description: Digital logic, assembly language, memory hierarchy, and processor architecture.

name: Operating Systems
description: Process management, threading, synchronization, memory management, and file systems.

name: Database Systems
description: Relational model, SQL, normalization, transactions, and database design.

name: Software Engineering
description: Software development lifecycle, requirements, design patterns, testing, and project management.

name: Computer Networks
description: Network protocols, TCP/IP stack, routing, security, and application-layer design.
